reason: Verification failed due to core misalignment with the spec: missing required entities and interactions, several required metrics absent or misnamed, and parameter naming divergence. With one iteration remaining, a focused, minimal-viable refactor can implement spec-conformant entities, wire key interactions, and complete the metrics to reach acceptance.

specific_areas: Implement minimal viable entities and wiring: Household (with norms), WorkplaceSchool, PublicVenue (with enforcement_strength and policy_mask_required), PolicyMaker (policy schedule), MediaSource (reach/tone/credibility), and multiple Retailers (inventory, restock_rate, price).
Add household influence to social dynamics and track household_id for all agents.
Model location-based contacts and policy enforcement; compute mandated vs compliant visits to support policy_noncompliance_rate.

Complete and correctly name required metrics: time_to_target_adoption_70, sustained_adoption_duration_above_70, policy_noncompliance_rate, mask_availability_rate (time series and endline), adherence_probability_mean, adoption_inequality_gini_income, and alias peak_adoption_rate.
Harmonize parameter names with the spec and provide a backward-compatibility mapping layer.
Refactor retailers to multiple entities with affordability logic (affordability_threshold_income_fraction) and basic price dynamics under scarcity; compute daily mask_availability_rate.
Fix evaluation API: keep adoption_rate_over_time as a time series in run(); have evaluate() return summary metrics with unambiguous names (e.g., adoption_rate_mean).
Seeded, reproducible schedules for policy and media; ensure performance remains acceptable for current scale.

task_understanding.adjustments: Treat the specification as binding: implement the exact required entities, interactions, and metric names. Prioritize spec alignment over new features.

data_analysis.adjustments: Compute all required metrics precisely: time-to-thresholds, sustained durations, adherence_probability_mean, mask_availability_rate, and adoption_inequality_gini_income (e.g., by income deciles). Ensure adoption_rate_over_time remains a time series in run().

model_planning.adjustments: Plan a minimal viable architecture: introduce lightweight classes for required entities and wire them into the daily step. Define a clear policy schedule interface and media broadcast function. Scope changes to what is necessary for verification to pass.

code_generation.adjustments: Implement new entities as small dataclasses or simple classes. Add household grouping and location pools. Introduce a parameter mapping layer for backward compatibility. Keep interfaces stable and document new/aliased parameters.

code_verification.adjustments: Add checks/tests to confirm presence and correct naming of required metrics, and that policy_noncompliance_rate = 1 - policy_compliance_rate. Validate that adoption_rate_over_time is a list/series. Run a short seeded simulation to sanity-check outputs.

simulation_execution.adjustments: Use a fixed RNG seed for reproducibility; ensure new entities are invoked each step (media broadcast, policy enforcement, retailer restock/sales). Monitor runtime; avoid O(n^2) operations.

result_evaluation.adjustments: In run(), return the full required metric set with spec-compliant names. In evaluate(), use summary metrics only (e.g., adoption_rate_mean, peak_adoption_rate, time_to_target_adoption_70) and avoid name/value mismatches.

feedback_generation.adjustments: Produce a concise change log: implemented entities, added metrics, parameter name harmonization map, and any deprecations. Note any intentional placeholders with clear TODOs if unavoidable.
